title: A route renamed in the refactor, left unresolved with a question for each observation it carried
summary: The value-object refactor of 190, with `POST /quotes` renamed to `POST /quote`. Its observations are a consumer's: no proof about the new route can stand in for the old one without a person saying the rename is intended. The tool leaves the old route unresolved, counts its four observations as removed and the new route's as new, and asks a person about each.

change.description: `Quote`'s amount, a `long` of cents, becomes a value object, `Money`, so `Quote(long cents, int quantity)` is now `Quote(Money amount, int quantity)`; `Pricing.total` reads `q.amount.cents()` where it read `q.cents`; the pure helper `Pricing.discount` (a tenth off ten items or more) is rewritten as an early return; and the route `POST /quotes` makes the quote with `new Money(cents)`. Nothing is meant to change: not the total, not the event the route sends, not what `Pricing.withQuantity` hands back. In this version the route's path is also `/quote`.

risk: A rename of a route breaks every client of the old path, and a tool that matched routes by their handler, or reused the old route's proof for the new one, would report the change as preserved.
explanation: Entry points are matched by their id, the method and path, as `observations --against` matches them, so `POST /quotes` has no counterpart and is unresolved, never proved against `POST /quote`. Its result, exception, status and event are each an obligation counted as removed, and each is a question for a person: approve it as removed, or it stays unresolved. No proof is looked up for it, so no cached result of the old route is reused.
resolution: Keep the old path, or approve the rename as an intended change to what the route's consumers observe.
notes: Checked by `jvmcontract compare`, which build.py runs as the B9 check of the shop app (`run_tool_compare`): the unpatched build against the patched one, twice under one fresh proof cache, the verdict read from the rerun and the page's output from the first run. The verdict is the subject's; the page lists every other part the run checked.

The joint example of `llm-dlc/loops/foundations.md`'s Phase 5, made an example: the app's sources are the fixture's `before` build (`lib/tests/fixtures/foundations/`), and the patch turns them into its `after` build with the route-change defect (`defects/route-change/`) overlaid. `lib/tests/compare.rs` holds `jvmcontract compare` to the same builds inline; this is the same run by build.py, with the app's tests run too.

Nothing in the run is written by hand. The entry points' external inputs (`cents`, `quantity`) are anchored by their observation specs, so no mapping is involved at the boundary. The kernel's relation between the old and new quotes (`old.q.cents == new.q.amount.cents`, `old.q.quantity == new.q.quantity`) is alignment's proposal, inferred from how the two constructors route their parameters into the fields; it stays *proposed*, its evidence the proof under its claim key, and since nothing external anchors a kernel method's inputs, a proved relation there is reported as proved and not as the intended one.

What stays unresolved in every example of the set, by name: `POST /quotes/text` (its string concatenation isn't modeled), `Quote#cents` moved to `Money#cents` (a method of a class the old build doesn't have) and `Quote#quantity`, whose receiver is made differently in the two versions (`Quote(long, int)` before, `Quote(Money, int)` now), which the regression check doesn't relate yet. Before the application-core merge (2026-11-08) it was refused as an instance method instead; the merge's check takes a receiver made by its constructor, of the same construction in both versions.

Run inline on 2026-11-07 (JDK 25.0.5), `jvmcontract compare` on the app compiled unpatched and patched, as build.py compiles it, and on the fixture's builds, with the same verdicts (the times are the fixture's): `POST /quotes` unresolved (no counterpart), 4 obligations removed and 4 new, 4 questions of the category observation change, no decision made; the kernel's `total`, `withQuantity` and `discount` verified. 0.3 s cold, 0.1 s warm.
The app's tests pass on this version: they call the handler, not the path.
provenance: Constructed for Phase 5 of `llm-dlc/loops/foundations.md` (the joint example, made an example under the numbers 190-199). Examples 190 to 196 share the refactor: 190 is the refactor alone, and 191 to 196 each add one of the fixture's defects to it.

references.title: Godlin and Strichman, Regression verification: proving the equivalence of similar programs (2013)
Barthe, Crespo and Kunz, Relational verification using product programs (2011)
